web_evidence.note: The authorized Riverhead excerpt contains Chapters 1 and 2. Its base narration is third person and shifts into characters' knowledge; the apparent first-person phrase in Chapter 1 occurs inside speech explicitly attributed to Chicken Hill's old women.

person_note: The controlling narration is shifting third person, ranging from character-focused free indirect discourse to broad omniscient historical commentary. Multiple interior Goodreads passages independently corroborate the authorized opening and whole-book POV descriptions. First- and second-person forms in the supplied quotations occur in character speech or universal aphorisms. The authorized opening also resolves the potentially contrary phrase 'my lips': it belongs to an explicitly attributed oral account by Chicken Hill's old women, embedded within third-person narration. Sources differ only in calling the narration limited versus omniscient, a focalization distinction that does not affect the THIRD label.
